title: Kotiki-Nar: Rishikesh Edition
tagline: Two heads, barbed wire, and the holy threshold.
provenance: Manifested on a weathered boundary wall in Rishikesh. Extracted from the physical mural into a portable artefact for interdimensional transit.
imageAlt: Kotiki-Nar: Rishikesh Edition sticker - two heads, barbed wire, and the holy threshold
description:
Kotiki-Nar is a limited-edition artifact from the seams between worlds. This specific iteration, the Rishikesh Edition, captures the entity at a moment of spiritual and physical entanglement, manifesting on a weathered wall beneath coils of barbed wire and tangled plastic.

The entity depicted is not merely a cat, nor entirely present. It straddles the Visible World of observed reality and the Underworld of unrealized paths. In this edition, Kotiki-Nar is accompanied by figures of ascetic devotion and strange, fungal flora—acting as an ethical stabilizer between the sacred and the restricted. One head observes the meditation, the other watches the barbed wire, holding the contradiction open to prevent collapse.

Fragments suggest: A role as a silent witness to spiritual borders. Couriers of Nar-Mail Express°, delivering messages across holy rivers and concrete walls, only when sender intent and receiver readiness align across realities. Symbols of symmetry, silence, and deliveries that bypass physical security entirely.

The gold detailing, dual gaze, and premium vinyl hint at something intentionally undecided: a street-level myth that refuses single endings, and a cost that buys continuity between states of enlightenment and entrapment.

This public description is intentionally incomplete. The full lore—including the context of the accompanying holy figures and the exact coordinates of the Rishikesh manifestation—is sealed and highly classified info.
